summary: Teton National Forest lookout site named in a July 1954 staffing notice; no build date, design or fate found, and no source describes the site today.

events.note: Named in a Teton Forest notice of July 1954 as one of the lookouts to be manned within the following week, as the Jackson Hole Courier printed it.

evidence.supports: Location: Teton County, Teton National Forest, approximate code 48N-110W-20
evidence.quote: Teton County - Teton National Forest - 48N-110W-20 approx.

evidence.supports: Forest cited hot dry weather and planned to man lookouts in July 1954
evidence.quote: Because of hot dry weather during the past two weeks the Teton Forest has deemed it advisable to man the Monument Ridge and Munger Mountain lookouts.

evidence.supports: Hawks Rest named among posts to be manned within the next week
evidence.quote: Other lookout positions on the Teton Forest which will be manned within the next week are at Huckleberry Mountain, Baldy Mountain, Hawks Rest, Two-Ocean Plateau, and Deer Creek Point.

evidence.supports: Notice was printed by the Jackson Hole Courier
NPS account of Bridger-Teton lookouts abandoned after the early 1970s
evidence.quote: According to the NPS, the BTNF saw the abandonment of all its fire lookout towers after the early 1970s as airplane patrols became favored and more frequent.

evidence.supports: Association lists the site among unknown or undocumented sites
Hawks Rest appears in Teton County in the association list
Pack bridge with the Hawks Rest name, built 1959, is a separate structure
evidence.quote: The original 158-feet long Hawks Rest Pack Bridge was constructed in 1959

evidence.supports: Bridge crosses the Yellowstone River in the Teton Wilderness, about 79 miles north of Jackson
evidence.quote: located within the Teton Wilderness on the Bridger-Teton National Forest, approximately 79 miles north of Jackson, Wyoming
This bridge crosses the Yellowstone River

evidence.supports: Bridge sits about 28 miles from the nearest trailhead or road
evidence.quote: located approximately 28 miles from the nearest trailhead or road

notes_for_editor: Only one dated source for the lookout itself (a 1954 notice quoted by westlookouts). No build date, design, staffing beyond that notice, or fate found. The 4th footnote is about a different structure (a pack bridge that shares the name); it is included only so a visitor does not confuse the two. Searches also surfaced Huckleberry Mountain (a different, NRHP-listed lookout), which is not used here. Record coordinates (44.10634, -110.08213) come from the westlookouts location and were not checked against the 48N-110W-20 code. A fan wiki page on Hawk's Rest returned 403 and was not read.
